6426-epipolar-encoder.md.summary: The Epipolar Encoder resolves 3D scale ambiguity by aggregating cross-view features along epipolar lines, unlike standard volume rendering that samples along rays.

6448-multi-view-epipolar-encoder.md.summary: The Multi-View Epipolar Encoder aggregates epipolar samples from multiple reference views using view-specific embeddings to disambiguate sample origins, extending the standard two-view encoder for scalable 3D reconstruction.

19017-plane-sweep-volume-psv.md.summary: Plane Sweep Volume is a 5D tensor encoding epipolar geometry by projecting input views onto depth planes, enabling efficient local processing by aligning adjacent camera rays.

4298-warp-based-sampling.md.name: Warp-based Sampling

4865-hierarchical-sampling.md.summary: Hierarchical sampling is a two-stage strategy for volume rendering that improves image quality by concentrating samples in regions of high geometric or color complexity, addressing the bottleneck of point sampling in neural radiance fields. 4868-hierarchical-density-adaptation.md.name: Hierarchical Density Adaptation
4868-hierarchical-density-adaptation.md.summary: Hierarchical Density Adaptation is a volume rendering sampling strategy that maintains constant frame rates by generating coarse density estimates on-the-fly via convolution, distinguishing itself from standard methods that rely on pre-allocated coarse grids.

7323-hu-et-al-density-based-sampling.md.name: Hu et al. Density-based Sampling
7323-hu-et-al-density-based-sampling.md.summary: Hu et al. Density-based Sampling optimizes NeRF rendering by using a single view-independent density field to restrict expensive network evaluations to geometrically relevant regions.

17467-density-guided-sample-filtering.md.summary: Density-guided Sample Filtering optimizes volumetric rendering by using a priority queue to evaluate expensive appearance networks only at valuable points, avoiding GPU branching issues near boundaries.

8860-ddnerf.md.name: DDNeRF
8860-ddnerf.md.summary: DDNeRF is a neural volume rendering method that improves sampling efficiency by modeling coarse density distributions as mixtures of truncated Gaussians rather than discrete piecewise-constant functions.

16798-hierarchical-volume-sampling.md.name: Hierarchical Volume Sampling
16798-hierarchical-volume-sampling.md.summary: Hierarchical volume sampling reduces computational cost by concentrating samples in high-density regions, differing from standard NeRF by using a single network or compact 3D volume for the fine stage.

14475-ray-direction-jitter.md.name: Ray Direction Jitter
14475-ray-direction-jitter.md.summary: Ray Direction Jitter improves learned rendering generalizability by adding sub-pixel noise to ray vectors, preventing overfitting to training directions while keeping rays within pixel boundaries.

7499-perspective-warping.md.summary: Perspective warping maps unbounded scenes to bounded space using PCA, enabling arbitrary camera trajectories and adaptive grid allocation unlike methods restricted to forward-facing or 360-degree views.

9796-mls-volume-reconstruction.md.summary: MLS Volume Reconstruction is a volume rendering technique that approximates a continuous scalar field and its gradients from discrete samples on regular or irregular grids using Moving Least Squares (MLS) approximation. 11155-interblock-interpolation.md.name: Interblock Interpolation
11155-interblock-interpolation.md.summary: Interblock Interpolation is a GPU volume rendering technique that achieves high data reduction by interpolating values from neighboring block samples rather than individual voxels.

11694-nearest-neighbor-sampling.md.summary: Nearest Neighbor Sampling assigns the value of the single closest grid sample, prioritizing speed over visual quality by producing piecewise constant results without blending multiple values.

13925-inverse-distance-weighting-interpo.name: Inverse Distance Weighting Interpolation
13925-inverse-distance-weighting-interpo.summary: Inverse Distance Weighting Interpolation estimates values via a weighted average of nearby samples, offering continuous, differentiable results that differ from nearest neighbor sampling by allowing arbitrary neighbor counts.

14935-linear-interpolation.md.name: Linear Interpolation
14935-linear-interpolation.md.summary: Linear interpolation approximates a continuous scalar field from discrete samples using weighted averages based on spatial proximity, offering computational simplicity and lower cost at the expense of discontinuous derivatives.

16228-kernel-based-resampling.md.name: Kernel-based Resampling
16228-kernel-based-resampling.md.summary: Kernel-based resampling approximates continuous volumetric fields from discrete samples by convolving data with localized weight functions, reducing aliasing artifacts inherent in nearest-neighbor sampling.

817-interpolation-schemes-for-volume-ren.name: Interpolation Schemes for Volume Rendering
817-interpolation-schemes-for-volume-ren.summary: Interpolation schemes approximate continuous scalar fields from discrete voxel samples to eliminate discretization artifacts, distinguished by their broad spectrum from zero-order box filters to high-order frequency-domain sinc resampling.

848-fast-tri-cubic-interpolation.md.summary: Fast tri-cubic interpolation is a GPU-based method that reduces computational cost by using separable tri-cubic B-splines to achieve higher-order continuity with only eight texture fetches.

861-adaptive-filter-size-for-rendering-t.summary: Adaptive Filter Size for Rendering Time Reduction reduces rendering time by dynamically selecting smaller interpolation filters for low-energy frequency components while maintaining image quality.

15870-general-cubic-spline-interpolation.summary: General cubic spline interpolation uses piecewise third-order polynomials parameterized by B and C to ensure continuous first derivatives, distinguishing it from fourth-order families by simplifying the parameter space.

15871-four-parameter-polynomial-family.m.summary: The four-parameter polynomial family is a set of fourth-order reconstruction filters that generalizes Catmull-Rom splines, offering second-derivative continuity unachievable with cubic splines.

3273-anisotropic-total-variation.md.name: Anisotropic Total Variation
3273-anisotropic-total-variation.md.summary: Anisotropic Total Variation is a regularization prior that enforces piecewise constant solutions with axis-aligned edges by minimizing absolute differences along principal axes, making it computationally cheaper than isotropic methods.

16025-complexity-dropout.md.summary: Complexity Dropout is a Gaussian Splatting regularization technique that probabilistically excludes complexity from densification scores to balance structural refinement with coverage.

12946-few-view-reconstruction-via-regula.summary: Few-View Reconstruction via Regularization mitigates artifacts in sparse neural rendering by applying geometric or semantic priors to guide optimization, unlike progressive methods that restrain model capacity.

16585-multi-view-consistency-supervision.summary: Multi-view Consistency Supervision enforces semantic and geometric consistency across viewpoints by supervising rendered colors against uncertainty-weighted pseudo-ground truth derived from map priors.

15152-s-nerf-confidence-components.md.summary: S-NeRF Confidence Components is a selective weighting mechanism that adapts supervision reliability by using geometry and reprojection metrics for backgrounds while restricting vehicles to RGB and SSIM confidences.

15188-depth-priors-and-initialization.md.summary: Depth Priors and Initialization initializes or regularizes NeRF geometry using external depth estimates, distinguishing itself by fusing perspective maps into canonical panoramas via deformable alignment before training.

8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-dept.summary: Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map initializes NeRF geometry by fusing perspective depth maps into a canonical panorama via deformable alignment, addressing single-view under-constrained optimization.

14220-depth-supervision.md.name: Depth Supervision
14220-depth-supervision.md.summary: Depth supervision improves geometry and reduces artifacts by applying external monocular depth priors to radiance fields, distinguishing itself by refining existing optimizations rather than relying on multi-view consistency.

19001-refined-depth-for-geometry-supervi.name: Refined Depth for Geometry Supervision
19001-refined-depth-for-geometry-supervi.summary: Refined Depth for Geometry Supervision is a lightweight depth-regularization objective that improves local sharpness and depth consistency by combining rendered depths with input images to derive a geometry-supervision loss.

20059-depth-regularized-fine-tuning.md.summary: Depth-Regularized Fine-Tuning refines 3D Gaussian Splatting primitives using ground truth depth maps to enhance geometric accuracy and reduce training time.

8941-multi-view-sds.md.summary: Multi-view SDS is a regularization method that solves the Janus problem by stitching multiple rendered views into a composite image to enforce geometric consistency during 3D optimization.

10636-specific-loss-formulations.md.name: Specific Loss Formulations
10636-specific-loss-formulations.md.summary: Specific Loss Formulations are objective functions optimizing neural radiance fields by directly leveraging rendered statistics or geometric priors, distinguishing them from methods relying on external generative models.

10377-nerf-xl-multi-gpu-distortion-loss..name: NeRF-XL Multi-GPU Distortion Loss
10377-nerf-xl-multi-gpu-distortion-loss..summary: NeRF-XL Multi-GPU Distortion Loss computes global geometric penalties across distributed GPUs by aggregating auxiliary variables and transmittance to account for the full ray's probability distribution.

14672-rate-distortion-optimization-loss..name: Rate-Distortion Optimization Loss
14672-rate-distortion-optimization-loss..summary: Rate-Distortion Optimization Loss trains NeRFs by balancing photometric accuracy against representation efficiency, distinguished by explicitly including rate and regularization terms alongside standard MSE.

15455-final-loss-function.md.name: Final Loss Function
15455-final-loss-function.md.summary: The Final Loss Function minimizes pixel-wise squared error between rendered and ground-truth colors, distinguishing itself by focusing exclusively on photometric fidelity without geometric priors.

8701-alignerf-training-objective.md.name: AligNeRF Training Objective
8701-alignerf-training-objective.md.summary: AligNeRF Training Objective replaces standard MSE with patch-based and VGG feature losses to preserve high-frequency details despite image misalignment.

16814-geometric-and-structural-regulariz.name: Geometric and Structural Regularization
16814-geometric-and-structural-regulariz.summary: Geometric and Structural Regularization imposes constraints on radiance fields to enforce physical plausibility and structural integrity, distinguishing itself by explicitly shaping density and color fields rather than focusing on pixel-level fidelity.

10454-adaptive-rendering-loss-regulariza.summary: Adaptive Rendering Loss Regularization is a few-shot NeRF method that aligns positional encoding frequencies with rendering loss via adaptive weighting, avoiding external modules or pre-training.

18913-livescene-loss-function.md.summary: The LiveScene Loss Function trains interactive radiance fields by combining rendering, focal, repulsion, variable, language, and smoothness losses to manage dynamic foreground-background ambiguity.

10894-s3im.md.name: S3IM
10894-s3im.md.summary: S3IM is a multiplex loss function for neural fields that captures non-local structural similarity by processing multiple data points collectively rather than individually.

11100-volumetric-supervision.md.name: Volumetric Supervision
11100-volumetric-supervision.md.summary: Volumetric Supervision trains neural networks for dynamic tomography by minimizing the discrepancy between predicted volumes and dense ground-truth reconstructions, unlike methods relying on geometric consistency.

13426-perceptual-loss.md.summary: Perceptual loss preserves structural content in stylized volume rendering by minimizing VGG feature distances, unlike Gram matrix losses that average out details.

12264-clip-direction-consistency.md.summary: CLIP Direction Consistency evaluates NeRF edit smoothness by measuring how well semantic change directions match between original and edited views, distinct from text-image alignment metrics.

13433-global-local-contrastive-learning..summary: Global-Local Contrastive Learning is a regularization strategy for text-driven NeRF stylization that ensures uniform style by combining global and local CLIP contrastive terms, overcoming directional-only and non-uniform limitations.

17051-view-invariant-contrastive-loss.md.summary: View-invariant Contrastive Loss regularizes generative NeRF latent codes to reflect 3D content variations independently of 2D viewpoints, preventing optimization instability.

17225-text-guided-scene-style-editing.md.summary: Text-guided scene style editing uses CLIP loss to apply text-driven styles to entire 3D scenes, ensuring multi-view consistency unlike single-image methods.

8869-progressive-and-dynamic-scene-growt.summary: Progressive and Dynamic Scene Growth adaptively expands model capacity and training data during optimization to balance resources with fidelity, distinguishing itself from static NeRF by dynamically allocating representational power to uncertain regions.

12795-nerf-as-an-auto-decoder.md.summary: NeRF as an Auto-Decoder shares network parameters across multiple scenes while using per-scene latent codes, enabling unconditional 3D generation and single-view reconstruction without per-scene optimization.

16544-encoder-decoder-training.md.summary: Encoder-Decoder Training trains an encoder and decoder to reconstruct images from 3D latent codes, generalizing to unseen environments unlike standard NeRF optimization.

17506-decode-scene.md.summary: Decode-Scene trains NeRFs in latent space by decoding rendered latents to RGB for loss computation, differing from Encode-Scene by lacking latent caching and requiring decoder differentiation.

18172-dlr-nerf-construction.md.summary: DLR-NeRF Construction is a network distillation method that decomposes low-rank NeRF weights into Tensor Train components to bridge low-rank approximation and quantization, preserving structural benefits for efficient compression.

11963-generative-latent-optimization.md.name: Generative Latent Optimization
11963-generative-latent-optimization.md.summary: Generative Latent Optimization jointly optimizes latent codes and neural network parameters to minimize reconstruction loss, functioning as a discriminator-less GAN that captures view-dependent variations without adversarial training.

16692-gan-inversion-encoder-and-optimiza.summary: GAN Inversion Encoder and Optimization inverts source views into a latent code grid to enable view synthesis, distinguished by its local coordinate system that remains robust to 2D rotations unlike global methods.

16716-gsn-inversion.md.summary: GSN Inversion optimizes a latent code grid to locally condition a radiance field, using a local coordinate system robust to rotations unlike global methods.

14030-adversarial-training-gan.md.name: Adversarial Training (GAN)
14030-adversarial-training-gan.md.summary: Adversarial Training uses a parallel discriminator to classify rendered images as real or fake, adding a game-theoretic loss that encourages photorealism and high-frequency detail to overcome the blurriness of standard pixel-wise reconstruction.

19342-lighting-prediction-network-traini.name: Lighting Prediction Network Training
19342-lighting-prediction-network-traini.summary: Lighting Prediction Network Training is a two-stage strategy using hybrid loss and adversarial supervision to predict street scene lighting, distinguishing itself by addressing depth ambiguity and encouraging photorealism.

10251-iron.md.name: IRON
10251-iron.md.summary: IRON is a neural inverse rendering pipeline that reconstructs high-quality 3D geometry and spatially varying materials from photometric images (multi-view images captured with a collocated flashlight and moving camera). 10611-instance-nerf.md.name: Instance-NeRF
10611-instance-nerf.md.summary: Instance-NeRF is a 3D instance segmentation pipeline that extends NeRF with an instance field to resolve multi-view inconsistent 2D masks without relying on 3D bounding volume priors.

10928-mimo-nerf.md.name: MIMO-NeRF
10928-mimo-nerf.md.summary: MIMO-NeRF accelerates neural rendering by replacing standard MLPs with multi-input multi-output networks that process grouped ray samples simultaneously, using self-supervised 3D consistency loss to resolve ambiguities without teacher networks.

11061-appearance-and-lighting-decomposit.name: Appearance and Lighting Decomposition
11061-appearance-and-lighting-decomposit.summary: Appearance and Lighting Decomposition decouples view-independent material properties from view-dependent lighting in neural radiance fields to enable physically plausible relighting and accurate modeling of specular surfaces.

9113-nerflight.md.name: NeRFLight
9113-nerflight.md.summary: NeRFLight is a grid-based neural radiance field that achieves real-time view synthesis with reduced memory by splitting the scene into regions sharing a single feature grid and using separate density decoders.

9273-neural-light-field-representations..name: Neural Light Field Representations
9273-neural-light-field-representations..summary: Neural Light Field Representations map camera rays directly to RGB values, bypassing volumetric ray-marching to enable novel view synthesis with significantly faster rendering speeds than Neural Radiance Fields.

9257-neural-light-field-nelf.md.name: Neural Light Field (NeLF)
9257-neural-light-field-nelf.md.summary: Neural Light Field maps camera rays directly to RGB values via a single network pass, enabling novel view synthesis orders of magnitude faster than NeRF by bypassing volumetric ray-marching.

17252-point-based-neural-light-field.md.name: Point-based Neural Light Field
17252-point-based-neural-light-field.md.summary: Point-based Neural Light Field predicts density and color for all sample points in a single pass for efficient batch rendering, differing from standard NeRF by avoiding 3D geometry-agnostic direct ray-to-color mapping.

17211-progressively-connected-light-fiel.name: Progressively-connected Light Field Network (ProLiF) Architecture
17211-progressively-connected-light-fiel.summary: ProLiF is a neural light field architecture that decouples geometry from lighting using progressively merged subnetworks to prevent overfitting and improve detail reconstruction.

17248-progressive-training-scheme.md.name: Progressive Training Scheme
17248-progressive-training-scheme.md.summary: Progressive Training Scheme incrementally merges independent subnetworks to prevent overfitting and ensure consistent geometry, distinguishing itself from direct MLP training by enforcing an inductive bias for accurate scene reconstruction.

9475-anisotropic-neural-representation-l.name: Anisotropic Neural Representation Learning
9475-anisotropic-neural-representation-l.summary: Anisotropic Neural Representation Learning (ANRL) is a method for neural volume rendering that models volumetric density and latent features as view-dependent functions using spherical harmonics (SH) to eliminate directional ambiguity. 10843-ref-nerf.md.summary: Ref-NeRF is a neural radiance field method that improves specular reflection representation by decoupling geometry from lighting and reparameterizing directional input using reflection vectors.

11505-convex-combination-color-decoder.m.summary: The Convex Combination Color Decoder decomposes view-dependent appearance into a view-dependent base component and a glossy reflection component, weighted by a geometry-derived coefficient. 11359-stensorrf.md.name: STensoRRF
11359-stensorrf.md.summary: STensoRRF is a differentiable volume rendering method using a single decomposed 4D tensor to enable high-quality novel view synthesis and relighting with faster convergence than standard NeRFs.

11364-ced-nerf.md.name: Ced-NeRF
11364-ced-nerf.md.summary: Ced-NeRF is a compact dynamic neural radiance field method using a high-resolution grid and canonical space to prevent overfitting artifacts while ensuring rapid convergence and efficient rendering.

11366-dynamic-and-deformable-fields.md.name: Dynamic and Deformable Fields
11366-dynamic-and-deformable-fields.md.summary: Dynamic and Deformable Fields extend static neural radiance fields by adding temporal or deformation parameters to model scenes that change over time or undergo non-rigid motion.

11353-neural-deformable-voxel-grid-ndvg..name: Neural Deformable Voxel Grid (NDVG)
11353-neural-deformable-voxel-grid-ndvg..summary: Neural Deformable Voxel Grid is a fast dynamic scene view synthesis method that replaces heavy MLPs with voxel-grid interpolation and explicitly models occlusion based on motion and time.

11355-dynamic-neural-radiance-fields-t-r.summary: TöRF is a dynamic neural radiance field method that reconstructs scenes by optimizing against raw Time-of-Flight phasors and RGB images, enabling high-fidelity novel-view synthesis from moving cameras without relying on processed depth maps.

16314-rotate-tiling-rt-method.md.summary: The Rotate-Tiling method is a parallel volume rendering compositing algorithm that allows arbitrary processor counts and initial image blocks, unlike the Block-Splitting method which requires powers of two.

9377-direct-send-compositing.md.summary: Direct Send Compositing is a parallel technique where processors exchange specific image tiles via all-to-all communication for local assembly, differing from hierarchical methods by avoiding tree structures.

12057-tiling-compositing.md.summary: Tiling Compositing is a parallel compositing strategy for distributed volume rendering where processing elements (PEs) hold tiles of the final image and pass partial results to adjacent PEs in a staggered, linear fashion to merge them into the final image. 16580-parallel-compositing.md.name: Parallel Compositing
16580-parallel-compositing.md.summary: Parallel Compositing partitions images into tiles and uses MPI_Alltoallv to exchange ray-casting fragments for local compositing, differing from other methods by its reliance on this collective communication pattern.

9364-parallel-rendering-hybrid-systems.m.name: Parallel Rendering (Hybrid Systems)
9364-parallel-rendering-hybrid-systems.m.summary: Parallel Rendering (Hybrid Systems) combines shared-memory and distributed-memory parallelism to render volume data, reducing communication overhead and memory limits of pure approaches by partitioning image and data space across multicore clusters.

7094-temporal-division-of-uniform-resolu.name: Temporal Division of Uniform Resolution Data
7094-temporal-division-of-uniform-resolu.summary: Temporal Division of Uniform Resolution Data is a parallelism strategy that distributes time-varying volume rendering tasks across processors by assigning unique time steps, avoiding spatial file decomposition to reduce preprocessing overhead.

10328-breakable-integrals.md.summary: Breakable integrals decompose volume rendering equations into segment-wise operations for efficient multi-GPU parallelization, distinguishing themselves by distributing the integral's mathematical structure rather than just data elements.

9032-gpu-buffer-upload-via-transfer-buff.summary: GPU Buffer Upload via Transfer Buffer uses OpenGL PBO ping-pong buffering to asynchronously stream volume data, decoupling uploads from rendering to prevent CPU stalls without relying on dedicated copy engines.

9054-gpu-asynchronous-streaming.md.summary: GPU Asynchronous Streaming uses separate OpenGL contexts to overlap data transfers with rendering, preventing GPU stalls and maintaining high utilization.

10166-asynchronous-pipeline-overlap.md.summary: Asynchronous Pipeline overlaps SSD reads, data transfers, and GPU rendering using multi-threading to hide I/O latency, allowing rendering to proceed while data is fetched.

17179-overlapped-implementation.md.name: Overlapped Implementation
17179-overlapped-implementation.md.summary: Overlapped Implementation hides data transfer overhead by using multi-threading and asynchronous I/O to render volume slices while data is still being fetched, unlike sequential methods.

14603-host-device-memory-transfer-with-e.summary: Host-Device Memory Transfer with Events precisely measures Host-to-Device and Device-to-Host transfer times and kernel latency by isolating these phases from CPU scheduling noise.

9704-multipass-partitioning-mpp.md.summary: Multipass Partitioning splits shader dependency graphs into multiple passes to fit resource-constrained GPUs, minimizing runtime while respecting hardware limits.

9735-dynamic-programming-multipass-parti.name: Dynamic Programming Multipass Partitioning
9735-dynamic-programming-multipass-parti.summary: Dynamic Programming Multipass Partitioning is a method that partitions shader dependency graphs into passes to minimize runtime while respecting resource constraints, guaranteeing global optimality unlike greedy approximations.

15956-dp-algorithm-configuration-selecti.name: DP Algorithm (Configuration Selection)
15956-dp-algorithm-configuration-selecti.summary: The DP Algorithm (Configuration Selection) determines the globally optimal rendering configurations for segmented objects under a strict memory budget, maximizing quality by reallocating resources from low-complexity to high-complexity objects.

11538-megakernel-generation.md.name: Megakernel Generation

10234-warp-subgroup-level-primitives.md.name: Warp/Subgroup Level Primitives
10234-warp-subgroup-level-primitives.md.summary: Warp/Subgroup Level Primitives enable fast, lockless thread communication and aggregation within a GPU execution unit using registers, bypassing global memory latency and shared memory bottlenecks.

3683-subgroup-operations.md.name: Subgroup Operations
3683-subgroup-operations.md.summary: Subgroup operations are fast, hardware-synchronized collective computations within a warp or wave that exchange data via registers, avoiding the latency of global memory synchronization used by atomic operations.

4949-warp-shuffling.md.name: Warp Shuffling
4949-warp-shuffling.md.summary: Warp Shuffling is a warp-level reduction technique using hardware shuffle instructions to keep data in registers, eliminating shared memory allocation and synchronization barriers.

5523-double-buffer-shuffling.md.name: Double Buffer Shuffling
5523-double-buffer-shuffling.md.summary: Double Buffer Shuffling is a warp-level reduction technique that splits workload across two halves of a warp using dual buffers to mitigate active thread reduction issues found in single-buffer approaches.

8113-double-buffer-shared-warp-marching..summary: Double Buffer Shared Warp Marching is a GPU volume rendering technique that uses two buffers per thread to keep the entire warp active during reduction, improving execution efficiency over previous methods.

10224-warp-level-reduction.md.name: Warp-level Reduction
10224-warp-level-reduction.md.summary: Warp-level reduction aggregates update requests within a GPU warp to minimize redundant atomic operations, distinguishing itself by focusing on contention reduction for atomic primitives.

13060-gpu-offloaded-calculations.md.name: GPU Offloaded Calculations

13356-gpu-matrix-operations.md.summary: GPU Matrix Operations offloads linear algebra computations like inversion and transformation from the CPU to the GPU, saving CPU cycles and focusing on the computational cost of rendering static voxel scenes.
